title: VIII–X. Exaltation: resurrection and ascension into heaven
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): resurrection, ascension into ye heavens, and session at ye right hand belonging toward God ye Father. — Ye state belonging toward exaltation embraces three principal degrees: — VIII. — We attribute this resurrection not only toward ye Father through ye Holy Spirit, but also toward Christ Himself as efficient cause, since He had power both toward lay down and toward take up again His soul (John 10:17-18). — Yet by an overflowing power He could also discharge ye offices belonging toward animal life toward as long as after ye resurrection He remained in this life with ye disciples toward win faith toward ye resurrection. — Resurrection stands as ye beginning belonging toward glory and liberation from ye bonds belonging toward hell and death, by which ye dead body belonging toward Christ, placed in ye tomb, with ye effects belonging toward death in it removed, was reunited toward His soul and recalled into life — not this animal life, but a spiritual one. — IX. — From this fountain stand as drawn certain solutions belonging toward ye sophisms by which some papal writers seem toward defend ye dogma belonging toward transubstantiation, and some ye dogma belonging toward consubstantiation, or belonging toward ye presence belonging toward Christ's body IN, with, and UNDER ye bread by substantial non-distance — an error that wiser men today do not acknowledge, as absurd. — Ye ascension belonging toward Christ into heaven stands as ye progress belonging toward His exaltation, by which, after He had administered on earth ye office enjoined on Him, He was taken up in His glorious body toward discharge in heaven and from heaven other offices necessary toward procuring ye salvation belonging toward men, and there He remains until He returns toward judgment. — X.
pass_b_english: VIII. The state of exaltation embraces three principal degrees: resurrection, ascension into the heavens, and session at the right hand of God the Father.

IX. Resurrection is the beginning of glory and liberation from the bonds of hell and death, by which the dead body of Christ, placed in the tomb, with the effects of death in it removed, was reunited to His soul and recalled into life — not this animal life, but a spiritual one. Yet by an overflowing power He could also discharge the offices of animal life for as long as after the resurrection He remained in this life with the disciples to win faith for the resurrection. We attribute this resurrection not only to the Father through the Holy Spirit, but also to Christ Himself as efficient cause, since He had power both to lay down and to take up again His soul (John 10:17-18).

X. The ascension of Christ into heaven is the progress of His exaltation, by which, after He had administered on earth the office enjoined on Him, He was taken up in His glorious body to discharge in heaven and from heaven other offices necessary for procuring the salvation of men, and there He remains until He returns for judgment. From this fountain are drawn certain solutions of the sophisms by which some papal writers seem to defend the dogma of transubstantiation, and some the dogma of consubstantiation, or of the presence of Christ's body IN, with, and UNDER the bread by substantial non-distance — an error that wiser men today do not acknowledge, as absurd.
source_text: VIII. Status vero exaltationis complectitur tres potissimum gradus: resurrectionem, ascensionem in caelos, & sessionem ad dextram Dei Patris. IX. RESURRECTIO est initium gloriae & liberatio a vinculis inferni et mortis, qua corpus Christi mortuum inque sepulchro positum, sublatis mortis in eo effectibus, animae suae reunium, & eo in vita, non hanc animalem, sed spiritualem, revocatum est. Etsi tamen & vi abundante animalis vitae munia obire potuerit, quamdiu post resurrectionem in hac vita cum discipulis ad fidem resurrectioni conciliandam commoratus fuerit. Hanc vero resurrectionem non tantum Patri per Spiritum S. verum etiam Christo ipsi, tanquam causae efficienti, tribuimus, quippe qui potestatem habuerit ut ponendi, ita & animam suam resumendi, Joh. 10:17-18. X. ASCENSIO Christi in caelum est exaltationis ipsius progressus, quo cum in terra munus iniunctum administrasset, corpore suo glorioso, ad alia munia saluti hominum procuranda necessaria in caelo ac de caelo obeunda, eo evectionus est, ibidemque permanet, donec ad iudicium reveniat. Ex hoc fonte hauriuntur quaedam solutiones sophismatum, quibus Pontifices quidam dogma de transsubstantiatione, & quidam dogma de consubstantiatione, sive praesentia corporis Christi IN, cum, & SUB pane per indistantiam substantialem defendere videntur, quem errorem tamen sapientiores ut absurdum hodie non agnoscunt.
